You are a repo fix worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the loop-factory repo (/mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory) at HEAD — edit files here directly.

OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY: you own exactly four paths: departments/podcast/runtime/compare_charter.py, departments/podcast/runtime/escalate_outbox.py, departments/podcast/tests/test_compare_charter.py, and departments/podcast/tests/test_escalate_outbox_copy.py (new file — if a test file for escalate_outbox already exists under departments/podcast/tests/, extend THAT instead and treat it as the owned fourth path; check first). Nothing else. Never touch .git, never commit, never run git add; leave changes uncommitted.

CONTEXT — a real owner complaint from today, verbatim spirit: the owner received this on his phone and had 'no clue what it means':
  '[podcast] needs you: hopper_blind: Hopper/publish-reliability evidence is unavailable — what broke the publish schedule source or the publish-day verifier?'
The pipeline: compare_charter.py classifies sensor observations into failure classes (FAILURE_CLASSES) with a per-sensor QUESTIONS map; escalate_outbox.py turns open incidents into outbox rows with an 'eli5' field; the mailroom renders eli5 into the Telegram buzz and the Linear card the owner acts on. The QUESTIONS text is written for engineers. The owner's standing instruction (2026-08-05): every escalation must lead with 'a simple message and bare bones on what it means and what it needs'.

CHANGE:
1. In compare_charter.py add a MEANINGS map: for EVERY failure class name that FAILURE_CLASSES (and FAILURE_HINT_CLASSES, if its classes differ) can produce, provide two short plain-English strings written for a busy non-technical owner: what_it_means (one sentence, no jargon — never use words like sensor, evidence, verifier, ledger, fingerprint, observation without explaining in plain terms what broke for HIM) and what_it_needs (one sentence: the concrete decision or repair being asked for, and who is expected to do it — 'ops repair, nothing needed from you unless you disagree' is a valid and often correct answer). Example for hopper_blind: what_it_means='The watchdog gauge that checks episodes are publishing on time has no data to read — the podcast itself may be fine, but this gauge is blind.', what_it_needs='An ops repair of the publish-schedule data file; nothing needed from you unless you want it handled differently.' Carry both strings into the candidate dict compare_observations builds.
2. In escalate_outbox.py, compose the outbox row so the human-facing text LEADS with the plain language: eli5 becomes '[podcast] <short plain headline> — WHAT THIS MEANS: <what_it_means> WHAT IT NEEDS: <what_it_needs>'. Keep the machine fields (issue, fingerprint, one_question, context) unchanged for downstream tooling — the technical one_question moves INTO context only, never the headline. Inspect how escalate_outbox builds rows today and keep every other behavior (dedup, marker files, TTL) identical.
3. Tests: (a) extend departments/podcast/tests/test_compare_charter.py — every failure class reachable from FAILURE_CLASSES has a non-empty what_it_means and what_it_needs, and neither contains the banned jargon words (sensor, verifier, fingerprint, observation) unaccompanied; keep it simple: assert the banned words are absent from what_it_means; (b) new test for escalate_outbox: a hopper_blind incident produces an outbox row whose eli5 starts with '[podcast]' and contains 'WHAT THIS MEANS:' and 'WHAT IT NEEDS:' and does NOT start with the raw failure-class token; and the row still carries the technical question in context.

HOW TO RUN (from the worktree root — all must pass): PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest departments/podcast/tests -q -p no:cacheprovider && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 loopfactory.py check

HARD RULES: no new dependencies, smallest diffs, do not change classification logic or severities, do not weaken the raise-on-unknown-pair guard, no reformatting of untouched lines, never invoke any network, model CLI, MCP, or skill, leave changes uncommitted. The coordinator handles the governed release re-pin.
